Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
516 PM EDT Thu Sep 3 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Severe T-Storm Watch is in effect for portions of western MD 
and the eastern WV midnight. Monitoring two clusters of storms:
one of which northwest of Pittsburgh and another back toward
Erie, PA/Cleveland. This activity will sag south and east beyond
7pm. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Slight Risk of severe thunderstorms today and Friday.

- 2) Hot and humid conditions will persist through Friday.

- 3) Drier conditions expected for the Labor Day weekend through
  early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Slight Risk of severe thunderstorms today and
Friday.

Clouds have readily thinned in the wake of morning shower and
thunderstorm activity. This is allowing for temperatures to rise
quickly through the 80s to near 90. This heating will play an
important role in the potential for severe weather through the
evening hours.

As of 2:30 PM, a few discrete (transient supercell)
thunderstorms had developed over the Shenandoah Valley, and had
a history of producing large hail and wind damage. These storms
are developing in an area that has been clear since daybreak, 
and in an area of enhanced low-level convergence due to residual
outflow from morning convection to the north, a washed out 
front, and terrain circulations. Anticipate this activity to 
continue into the late afternoon hours with a risk of localized 
damaging wind gusts and large hail.

Meanwhile, upstream over the lower Great Lakes and Ohio Valley,
a large reservoir of MLCAPE 3000-4000+ J/kg exists. The north
end of this CAPE pool lies along the southern edge of the
westerlies, with a 100+ kt 300 hPa jet streak and mid-level
shortwave impulse located just to the north. This setup is
favorable for the development of a Mesoscale Convective Complex
(MCS), which is an organized line of thunderstorms that persists
for several hours.

Locally, mid-level lapse rates of 6.5-7 C/km (per latest
mesoanalysis and the KIAD 12Z RAOB) atop a very moist boundary
layer with surface dew points well into the 70s F will lead to
increasing CAPE despite the late start at surface heating. The
question then becomes just how organized upstream storms become,
and how stable the boundary layer is heading further into the
evening. A more organized and potent line of storms a bit
earlier in the evening would result in a notably higher risk for
more numerous damaging wind gusts, especially focused along the
residual baroclinic zone/theta-e gradient which should lie near
the Potomac River/US-50/I-66 this evening. A somewhat slower
and/or more disorganized line would result in a lower risk for
severe surface gusts, though some isolated damaging winds would
still be possible given high CAPE/DCAPE and the shallow nature 
of the stable layer near the surface. Areas of western Maryland
and perhaps into the eastern West Virginia panhandle are most
likely to see the storms prior to the onset of appreciable
nocturnal boundary layer stability.

The area remains in a Slight Risk (level 2 out of 5) for severe
weather from SPC as of the midday outlook update, driven mostly
by the threat of damaging wind gusts. There is a threat for
large hail in stronger cores, though mid-level lapse rates will
gradually become less steep tonight. A linear storm mode would
tend to be less favorable for large hail production (as opposed
to discrete/individual cells), as well. A few discrete cells 
are possible this evening in weak low-level WAA, however, 
independent of any linear system that may affect the region.
These storms would be most likely to develop over northern and
central Virginia into central Maryland along a weak surface
trough and the aforementioned moisture/instability gradient.

In the event an organized MCS develops, and/or cells form ahead
of and merge (either with each other, or the convective complex),
then some training or repeat activity would be possible
especially on its southwestern flank. This threat is far too
conditional for a watch at the moment, but is a possibility to
be monitored into the night.

Additional showers and thunderstorms, possibly strong to severe,
are anticipated again on Friday. Timing is a bit uncertain given
the subtle waves aloft, but increasing low-level convergence
paired with another upper impulse may very well result in
another round or two of storms with a damaging wind risk. The
latest guidance has nudged the threat a bit further north,
encompassing areas as far north as I-70 or the Mason-Dixon line
(as opposed to I-66/US-50). This will depend on any residual
early day clouds or convection, of course.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions will persist through
Friday.

Temperatures in the upper 80s to lower 90s and dew points in the
lower to middle 70s will result in heat indices in the upper 90s
to lower 100s each afternoon through Friday, just shy of Heat
Advisory criteria for most (except around Charlottesville and
surrounding Albemarle/Nelson Counties). The potential for early
day clouds to offset heating precludes enough confidence to
issue any further heat headlines at this time, though it will be
unusually hot and humid for early September regardless.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Drier conditions expected for the Labor Day weekend 
through early next week.

A high pressure system over the Great Lakes continues to track 
southeastward towards our forecast region through Tuesday. Over this 
time period, condtions remain predominantly dry, apart from 
 an isolated shower in the Appalachian mountains. 

Temperatures remain seasonable for early September this weekend, 
with temperatures rising above normal by Tuesday. Moist and warmer 
conditions return as we head into the middle of next week. Warm, 
moist air at the surface could lead to unstable conditions, with 
chances for showers and thunderstorms returning by late Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /21Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Have shifted PROB30s to this evening for most TAF sites
(slightly earlier at KMRB but still mainly late this evening
01-05z/9pm-1am). This appears to be the highest chance for 
storms, though some lead activity to develop especially near 
KCHO a bit earlier).

Winds will vary between W and SW as a surface trough develops
overhead with speeds generally AOB 10 kts. Guidance is not keen
on low clouds or fog overnight into early Friday, though the
pattern would suggest at least some conditional potential.

Additional storms with somewhat uncertain timing are possible
Friday. Was too low on confidence in timing for 18Z TAFs, but
PROB30s are likely to be included in subsequent updates, focused
probably on the typical peak diurnal window (~19Z-01Z). Winds
will shift to NW by late Friday through Saturday.

This weekend, prevailing VFR conditions are expected across all 
terminals and are expected to continue into early next week. 
Light northeasterly winds on Sunday shift easterly by Monday.

&&

.MARINE...
Special Marine Warnings may be needed this evening as storms
develop and track towards the waters. Additional storms are
anticipated on Friday, most likely late afternoon and evening.
Otherwise, generally light flow is expected into the upcoming
weekend, though NW gusts could approach SCA levels Friday night
into Saturday.

On Sunday and Monday, wind gusts remain below SCA-criteria with 
highest chances for approaching SCA thresholds Sunday afternoon or 
evening. Light northeasterly winds on Sunday shift easterly by 
Monday.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...Heat Advisory until 7 PM EDT this evening for VAZ036-037.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...DHOF/KVH
AVIATION...DHOF/KVH
MARINE...DHOF/KVH
